coverageNotes: Partial Pennsylvania candidate coverage: Philadelphia City Commissioners states “On November 03, 2026, Philadelphia voters will cast Election ballots to select candidates for the following offices:” Its list and the official York and Allegheny county general-election files provide 68 contests and 105 printed candidacies. Congressional districts 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, and 17, six state Senate districts, and 54 state House districts are held. Candidates in the other Pennsylvania districts remain to be acquired.

The statewide Candidate Database linked by the Pennsylvania Department of State returned an Incapsula page stating “Request unsuccessful.” The saved response supplied no candidate list. The Department states: “To obtain electronic copies of nomination petitions, please visit the Candidate Database or email your request to ra-elections@pa.gov.”
The Philadelphia candidate list is the current official November 3 general-election listing, but it does not explicitly label itself certified; candidateListComplete remains false.

Statewide measures remain unverified. The official ballot-question file linked by Philadelphia is titled “PROPOSED CHARTER CHANGE QUESTION” and contains two Philadelphia Home Rule Charter questions. It is a county document and cannot establish that Pennsylvania has no statewide measures. A statewide measure list or official no-measure statement remains to be acquired.
The statewide ticket names are preserved as the joint candidacies printed on the ballot. Incumbency and candidate websites are not stated in the saved list.

York County states “Note: This list is unofficial and subject to change.” Allegheny County states “This list will be updated as candidates continue to file petitions, nomination papers and filing fees.” Both county files remain incomplete-certification coverage, with candidateListComplete false.
